page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the E2 machine family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The underlying hardware features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. This configuration consists of 1 physical core supporting hyper-threading with 2 threads per core, backed by a dedicated CPU allocation. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 55 MB of L3 cache.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the e2-standard-2 operates in the lower performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng yields a score of 1103.39, while multi-core performance reaches 1451.58, placing the instance in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 79.92 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drop to 11.77 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect lower-tier performance, with a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 18.58 GB/sec and a Geekbench single-core score of 867.0.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or a GPU, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its hardware profile and lower benchmark results, such as a static web serving throughput of 1.45 GB/sec and a Redis SET rate of 1.35 million operations per second, the e2-standard-2 is best suited for lightweight workloads. These include basic web serving, small-scale development environments, low-traffic database operations, and simple background utility tasks where high-compute throughput is not required.
